questions.question: Which of the following pairs of years have identical calendars?
questions.solution:
Let us check the pair **2011** and **2022**:

Year **2011** is an **ordinary year** (not divisible by 4).

Year **2022** is an **ordinary year** (not divisible by 4).

Both are of the same type.

The odd days for each year are as follows:

 
• 2011 (Ordinary Year) = **1**
 
• 2012 (Leap Year) = **2**
 
• 2013 (Ordinary Year) = **1**
 
• 2014 (Ordinary Year) = **1**
 
• 2015 (Ordinary Year) = **1**
 
• 2016 (Leap Year) = **2**
 
• 2017 (Ordinary Year) = **1**
 
• 2018 (Ordinary Year) = **1**
 
• 2019 (Ordinary Year) = **1**
 
• 2020 (Leap Year) = **2**
 
• 2021 (Ordinary Year) = **1**

Total odd days = 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 = **14**

Since 14 ÷ 7 = 2 with a **remainder of 0**, the sum of odd days is a multiple of 7.

Therefore, the calendar of **2011** and **2022** will be identical.

Checking other options:

**2017 and 2027:** Total odd days = 12 (Not a multiple of 7).

**2003 and 2007:** Total odd days = 5 (Not a multiple of 7).

**2014 and 2020:** 2014 is an ordinary year while 2020 is a leap year (Different types).

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 1**”.

questions.question: A watch is 12 minutes slow at 4 AM. It gains 48 seconds every hour. When will it show the correct time (in PM) again?
questions.solution:
The watch is slow by 12 minutes at **4 AM**.

To show the correct time, the watch must gain 12 minutes.

Total time to gain in seconds = 12 × 60 = **720 seconds**

The watch **gains 48 seconds** every hour.

Number of hours required to gain 720 seconds = 720 ÷ 48

Required time = **15 hours**

Now, we add 15 hours to the starting time of 4 AM:

4 AM + 12 hours = 4 PM

4 PM + 3 hours = **7 PM**

The watch will show the **correct time** at **7:00 PM**.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 1**”.

questions.question: The ratio of present ages of two persons is 2 : 5. The sum of their ages is 21. What will be the ratio of ages of the two persons after 7 years from present?
questions.solution:
Given that the **ratio of present ages** of two persons is **2 : 5**.

Let the present ages of the two persons be **2x** and **5x** respectively.

The **sum of their present ages** is given as **21**.

2x + 5x = 21

7x = 21

x = 21 ÷ 7

x = 3

Present age of the first person = 2 × 3 = **6 years**

Present age of the second person = 5 × 3 = **15 years**

Age of the first person after 7 years = 6 + 7 = **13 years**

Age of the second person after 7 years = 15 + 7 = **22 years**

The **required ratio** of their ages after 7 years = **13 : 22**

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 1**”.

questions.question: Which Hindu epic narrates the story associated with Dashara?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ramayana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dashara**, also known as **Vijayadashami**, is a major Hindu festival celebrated at the end of **Navaratri** every year.
 
• The **Ramayana**, traditionally attributed to the sage **Valmiki**, is the primary scripture that narrates the life and exploits of **Lord Rama**, the prince of **Ayodhya**.
 
• The festival commemorates the day **Lord Rama** killed the ten-headed demon king **Ravana**, who had kidnapped **Sita**, Rama's wife.
 
• The victory signifies the triumph of **Dharma** (righteousness) over **Adharma** (evil) and is celebrated on the 10th day of the **Ashwin** month in the Hindu calendar.
 
• In many parts of India, large effigies of **Ravana**, **Kumbhakarna**, and **Meghnad** are burned to symbolize the destruction of evil forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahabharata**:

 
 
• An ancient Indian epic attributed to **Sage Vyasa**, centered on the struggle between two groups of cousins, the **Kauravas** and the **Pandavas**.
 
• It is the longest epic in the world and contains the **Kurukshetra War**, though some regional traditions also link the **Pandavas** returning from exile to the day of **Dashara**.
 
 
 
• **Bhagavad Gita**:
 
 
• A 700-verse Hindu scripture that is part of the **Mahabharata**, specifically the **Bhishma Parva**.
 
• It presents a dialogue between **Lord Krishna** and **Arjuna** regarding the nature of duty, soul, and **Moksha**.
 
 
 
• **Vedas**:
 
 
• The oldest layer of **Sanskrit literature**, consisting of the **Rigveda**, **Samaveda**, **Yajurveda**, and **Atharvaveda**.
 
• They are religious texts containing hymns, incantations, and rituals rather than narrative historical epics like the **Ramayana**.

questions.question: The Peninsular Plateau of India is primarily composed of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Igneous and metamorphic rocks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Peninsular Plateau** is one of the oldest and most stable landmasses of the Earth, having been formed from the breaking and drifting of the ancient **Gondwana land**.
 
• It is primarily composed of ancient **crystalline igneous** and **metamorphic rocks**, which date back to the **Pre-Cambrian** era, representing the stable **Indian Shield**.
 
• The plateau is characterized by broad and shallow valleys and rounded hills, with its foundation consisting of **Archean** gneisses and schists that have undergone extensive transformation over billions of years.
 
• The region is divided into two broad categories: the **Central Highlands** (north of the Narmada River) and the **Deccan Plateau** (south of the river), both of which share this fundamental geological composition.
 
• The rocks in this region, such as **Granite** and **Gneiss**, are highly durable and have been subjected to significant **tectonic** and **denudational** processes over geological time.

questions.question: As of August 2025, NASA confirmed nearly ____ exoplanets.
questions.solution:

__
 
• As of **August 2025**, the official **NASA Exoplanet Archive** confirmed that the number of discovered alien worlds outside our solar system has surpassed the **6,000** mark.
 
• This milestone follows the previous record of **5,000 confirmed exoplanets**, which was officially reached in **March 2022**, indicating a consistent discovery rate of several hundred planets per year.
 
• The primary driver for these discoveries is the **Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS)** mission, which has identified thousands of **TESS Objects of Interest (TOIs)** that were later validated as confirmed planets.
 
• A significant portion of these confirmations results from the legacy data of the **Kepler Space Telescope** and the **K2** mission, processed using advanced **Machine Learning** and **Artificial Intelligence** algorithms to distinguish real planets from stellar noise.
 
• Confirmation of an exoplanet typically requires detection by at least two different methods or multiple observations by independent telescopes to verify its **orbital period** and **mass**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NASA Missions and Facilities**:

 
 
• **James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)**: Launched in late **2021**, it focuses on the atmospheric characterization of these **6,000** worlds, searching for biosignatures like **methane** and **water vapor**.
 
• **Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope**: Expected to launch by **2027**, it will use **Gravitational Microlensing** to find thousands more planets in the **Milky Way**.
 
 
 
• **Detection Methodologies**:
 
 
• **Transit Method**: Measures the dimming of a star; responsible for over 75 percent of all confirmed exoplanets.
 
• **Radial Velocity**: Detects the gravitational tug a planet exerts on its host star, causing a detectable **Doppler shift**.
 
 
 
• **Planet Classifications**:
 
 
• **Super-Earths**: Planets larger than Earth but smaller than **Neptune**; they are the most common type of planet found in the current catalog.
 
• **Goldilocks Zone**: The region around a star where conditions are favorable for **liquid water**, a key focus for researchers studying the latest discoveries.

• **Chandrayaan-1** was India's inaugural lunar exploration mission, launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** to study the lunar surface.
 
• The spacecraft was launched on **October 22, 2008**, from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC)** at **Sriharikota**, Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The probe was launched using the **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV-C11)** and carried eleven scientific instruments intended for chemical, mineralogical, and photo-geologic mapping of the Moon.
 
• Communication with the **Chandrayaan-1** spacecraft was unexpectedly lost at **01:30 IST** on **August 29, 2009**, after the probe had completed over **3,400 orbits** around the Moon.
 
• Following the loss of radio signals, the mission was officially declared concluded by **ISRO** on **August 30, 2009**, after approximately **312 days** in operation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• The **Moon Impact Probe (MIP)**, an Indian-built instrument, successfully separated from the orbiter and struck the lunar surface near the **Shackleton Crater** on **November 14, 2008**.
 
 
 
• **Post-Mission Developments**:
 
 
• In **March 2017**, **NASA** scientists successfully relocated the derelict **Chandrayaan-1** spacecraft in a polar orbit approximately **200 kilometers** above the lunar surface using ground-based radar.
 
• The mission paved the way for subsequent lunar explorations, including **Chandrayaan-2** in **2019** and the successful soft landing of **Chandrayaan-3** in **August 2023**.

⇒ 41: Not divisible by 2, 3, 5, or 7. (**Prime**)

⇒ 42: Even number. (**Composite**)

⇒ 43: Not divisible by 2, 3, 5, or 7. (**Prime**)

⇒ 44: Even number. (**Composite**)

⇒ 45: Divisible by 5. (**Composite**)

⇒ 48: Even number. (**Composite**)

⇒ 49: Divisible by 7 (7 × 7). (**Composite**)

⇒ Sum = 41 + 43 + 47

⇒ Sum = 131

**∴ The correct answer is 131.**

Prime Numbers

A **prime number** is a natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two distinct factors: 1 and itself. The smallest prime number is **2** (the only even prime).

A **composite number** has more than two factors. For example, 49 is composite because its factors are 1, 7, and 49.

questions.question: G travels from P to Q. H travels from Q to P. They start travelling at the same time. Distance between P and Q is 500 km. They meet at point S after 5 hours. Speed of G is 60 km/hr. What is the speed (in km/hr) of H?

**∴ The correct answer is 40 km/hr.**

⇒ Distance covered by **G** in 5 hours = Speed × Time

⇒ Distance (G) = 60 × 5 = 300 km

⇒ Distance (H) = 500 − 300 = 200 km

If two objects start at the same time and meet, the time taken by both to reach the meeting point is identical.

questions.question: Marked price of an article is Rs. X. A person purchased it for Rs. Y after a discount of 40 percent on marked price. He then sold it for Rs. Z. If Z is 30 percent more than Y, then what is the ratio of Z to X?

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
She had sold the house years before the real estate boom.

options.text: The house has been sold by her years before the real estate boom.
The house was sold by her years before the real estate boom.
The house had been sold by her years before the real estate boom.
The house had sold by her years before the real estate boom.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The house had been sold by her years before the real estate boom.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence is in the **Active Voice** and uses the **Past Perfect Tense**. The structure of the sentence is: **Subject (She)** + **had** + **V3 (sold)** + **Object (the house)** + **Adverbial Phrase (years before the real estate boom)**.

• To transform a sentence from **Active Voice** to **Passive Voice** in the **Past Perfect Tense**, the following structural formula is applied: **New Subject (Object of Active)** + **had** + **been** + **V3 (Past Participle)** + **by** + **New Object (Subject of Active)**.

• The **Object** of the active sentence, **the house**, shifts to the **Subject** position in the passive sentence.

• The auxiliary verb **had been** must be used to maintain the **Past Perfect** aspect while indicating the **Passive Voice**.

• The main verb **sold** remains in its **Past Participle (V3)** form, which is standard for all passive constructions.

• The **Subject** of the active sentence, **She**, is converted into its **Objective Case** pronoun, which is **her**, and is preceded by the preposition **by**.

• The prepositional phrase **years before the real estate boom** remains unchanged as it provides the temporal context for the action.

 **Additional Information__**

• Understanding the tense discrepancies in the incorrect options:

• **Present Perfect Passive**: Option 1 uses **has been sold**. This is the **Present Perfect** form, which indicates an action connected to the present, whereas the original sentence describes an action completed before another past event.

• **Simple Past Passive**: Option 2 uses **was sold**. While this is a past tense, it fails to capture the **Past Perfect** nuance (the past of the past) established by **had sold**.

• **Structural Incompleteness**: Option 4 uses **had sold** in a passive-looking structure but omits the word **been**. Without **been**, the sentence does not function as a passive construction and remains grammatically incorrect in this context.

• **Pronoun Transformation**: In English grammar, when the subject **She** (nominative) moves to the object position (after **by**), it must always change to **her** (accusative).

</ul

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The school authorities organise the annual science exhibitions with great enthusiasm.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The provided sentence is in the **Passive Voice** and follows the structure of the **Simple Present Tense**: **Object + is/am/are + V3 (Past Participle) + by + Agent**.

• In the passive sentence, **The annual science exhibitions** acts as the object receiving the action, and **the school authorities** is the agent performing the action.

• To convert the sentence into the **Active Voice**, the agent **the school authorities** must be shifted to the **Subject** position at the beginning of the sentence.

• The verb phrase **are organised** (passive form) is converted to the **Active Verb** form **organise**. Since the new subject **the school authorities** is **plural**, the verb follows the **Subject-Verb Agreement** rule for the simple present tense without the suffix -s or -es.

• The original subject **The annual science exhibitions** is moved to the **Object** position, appearing immediately after the main verb.

• The prepositional phrase **with great enthusiasm** remains at the end as an **Adverbial Modifier** to retain the original context and manner of the action.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Active vs. Passive Voice Fundamentals**:

• **Active Voice**: The subject of the sentence performs the action. Structure: **Subject + Verb + Object**. It is generally more direct and concise.

• **Passive Voice**: The subject of the sentence is the recipient of the action. Structure: **Object + form of be + V3 + by + Agent**. It is used when the actor is unknown or less important than the action itself.

• **Tense Preservation in Voice Conversion**:

• **Simple Present**: Active (**V1/V1+s/es**) changes to Passive (**is/am/are + V3**).

• **Present Perfect**: Active (**has/have + V3**) changes to Passive (**has/have + been + V3**). Option 2 uses a form of this tense, which is incorrect here.

• **Past Perfect**: Active (**had + V3**) changes to Passive (**had + been + V3**). Option 3 uses this tense, which changes the timeline of the original sentence.

• **Simple Future**: Active (**will + V1**) changes to Passive (**will + be + V3**). Option 4 incorrectly shifts the meaning to the future.

</ul

Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

They are lacking ____ minimum courtesy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**in**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **lacking** in this sentence functions as an **adjective** (or a present participle used as an adjective) meaning deficient in or not having enough of something.
 
• Standard English grammar requires the preposition **in** to follow the adjective **lacking** when specifying the quality or attribute that is missing.
 
• Common idiomatic expressions include being **lacking in confidence**, **lacking in resources**, or **lacking in courtesy**.
 
• **Options 1, 3, and 4** do not follow the standard idiomatic usage with the word **lacking** in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *'They are **lacking in**__ minimum courtesy.'*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Lack (Verb):** When **lack** is used as a verb, it is transitive and takes no preposition. Example: 'They **lack** basic manners.'
 
• **Lack (Noun):** When **lack** is used as a noun, it is usually followed by the preposition **of**. Example: 'There is a **lack of** courtesy in their behavior.'
 
• **Lacking (Adjective):** When **lacking** is used as an adjective (following a form of the verb 'to be'), the preposition **in** is the correct choice. Example: 'He is **lacking in** experience.'

options.text: Why am I confused is because
The reason for my confusion is because

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I am confused because**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence contains a **redundant** expression, also known as a **pleonasm**. The phrase **the reason** and the **subordinating conjunction** **because** both indicate **causality**. Using them together in a single clause is considered **tautological** in standard English.
 
• The word **reason** acts as a noun that points to a cause, while **because** introduces the cause itself. Grammatically, 'the reason' should be followed by a **complement clause** starting with **that** (e.g., 'The reason is that...'), not an adverbial clause starting with 'because'.
 
• Option 3, **I am confused because**, provides the most **direct** and **concise** way to convey the message. It eliminates the **wordiness** of the original sentence by removing the unnecessary subject phrase 'The reason why'.
 
• In **Sentence Improvement** tasks, the goal is to choose the option that is both **grammatically accurate** and **stylistically superior**. Simplifying the structure to **Subject + Verb + Conjunction** ensures clarity and follows the **principle of economy** in language.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• Analysis of incorrect options:
 
 
• **Why am I confused is because**: This option incorrectly uses an **interrogative word order** ('Why am I') within a **declarative sentence**. Furthermore, it retains the **redundancy** between 'Why' and 'because'.
 
• **The reason for my confusion is because**: While it replaces 'why I am confused' with a **noun phrase**, it fails to correct the fundamental **grammatical error** of pairing 'reason' with 'because'. A correct alternative would have been 'The reason for my confusion is **that**'.
 
• **Redundancy Rule**: Common redundant phrases often tested include 'return back', 'reason why... because', 'repeat again', and 'sufficient enough'. Removing the repetitive element is a standard **error detection** strategy.
 
• **Conjunction usage**: **Because** is a **subordinating conjunction** that connects a dependent clause to an independent clause. When the purpose of the sentence is to state a fact directly, starting with the subject is preferred over complex **nominalizations**.
